parts:
Good morning everyone, 
here I am,using again nible to study population trends of amphibians!

I am preparing an occupancy model to estimate trends of occupancy for some amphibian species. I realized that including spatial autocorrelation is a fundamental step, hence I added an ICAR model that estimates a spatial random effect.

The model works, but I get this warning: "Warning: R object of different size than NimArrDouble. R obj has size 1 but NimArrDbl has size 20." and I can't find a way to understand where is the error. I can just tell you that "20" is the dimension of the primary periods (years / sampling seasons).
I attach the data for one of the species and paste the script below, hoping that you can help me to discover where the error is.

All the best, 
Mattia

library(nimble)

model <- nimbleCode({
 
  # Prior for the variance of CAR model
  psi_tau ~ T(dnorm(0, sd = 10), 0, ) # Truncated normal distribution with mean 0 and SD = 10
  # Spatial effect - CAR model
  psi_rho[1:nsite] ~ dcar_normal(adj=adj[1:sumneigh],weights=weights[1:sumneigh],num=num_adj[1:nsite],tau=psi_tau, zero_mean = 1)
 
  # Model for occupancy
  for (k in 1:nyear){
    for (i in 1:nsite){
    logit(psi[i,k]) <- alpha + beta.trend*year[k] + eps.year[k] + psi_rho[i]
    }
    eps.year[k] ~ dnorm(0, tau.lpsi) # Year random effect
  }
  alpha <- logit(mean.psi)
  mean.psi ~ dunif(0,1)
  beta.trend ~ dnorm(0, 0.01)
  tau.lpsi <- pow(sd.lpsi, -2)
  sd.lpsi ~ dunif(0, 10)

  # Ecological submodel
  for (i in 1:nsite){
    for (k in 1:nyear){
      z[i,k] ~ dbern(psi[i,k])
    }
  }
 
  # Priors for observational model
  p_int   ~ dnorm(0, 0.01)
  # Observational model
  for (i in 1:nsite){
    for (k in 1:nyear){
      for (j in 1:Tf[i,k]){ # Apply only to Tf[i,k] to avoid estimation of NA surveys
        muy[i,j,k] <- z[i,k]*p[i,j,k]
        logit(p[i,j,k]) <- p_int  
        y[i,j,k] ~ dbern(muy[i,j,k])
      }
    }
  }
 
  # Derived parameters
  for (k in 1:nyear){
    occ[k] <- sum(z[1:nsite,k]) # Occupancy in each year
  }
 
})

# Load data
load("dataset_occupancy.Rdata")

# Exclude NA in secondary periods
Tf <- matrix(1, nrow = dim(tab)[1], ncol = dim(tab)[3])
for (i in 1:nrow(Tf)){
  for(k in 1:ncol(Tf)){
    m <- max(which(is.na(tab[i,,k]) == FALSE))
   
    if(m != "-Inf"){ Tf[i,k] <- m}
  }
}

# FORMATTING DATA
win.data <- list(y = tab)
constants  <- list(nsite = dim(tab)[1], nyear = dim(tab)[3],
                   year = years-mean(c(min(years),max(years))),
                   adj = adiacenti,num_adj = num_adiacenti, sumneigh = sumneigh, weights = rep(1,sumneigh))

## RUN THE MODEL
# Parameters to monitor
params <- c("alpha","beta.trend","eps.year","sd.lpsi","occ","psi.trend",
            "p_int", "psi_tau","psi_rho")

# inits
inits <-list(alpha = rnorm(1,0,1), beta.trend = rnorm(1,0,1),
             eps.year = rnorm(1,0,1), sd.lpsi = dunif(1,0,10),
             p_int = rnorm(1,0,1),
             psi_tau=runif(1,1,10),psi_rho=runif(dim(tab)[1],-1,1))


# MCMC
nc <- 3 # Numero di catene
ni <- 6*10^3 # Numero di iterazioni
nb <- ni*2/3 # Burn-in
nt <- (ni-nb)/1000 # Thinning (in modo da avere 1000 posteriors)

# nimble model
Rmodel <- nimbleModel(code=model, constants=constants, data=win.data, inits = inits)
Rmodel$initializeInfo()
# mcmc
conf <- configureMCMC(Rmodel, print = F)
conf$addMonitors(c("alpha","occ", "psi_tau")) #, "psi.trend"
Rmcmc <- buildMCMC(conf) #,enableWAIC = TRUE)
# Compile the model and MCMC algorithm
Cmodel <- compileNimble(Rmodel)
Cmcmc <- compileNimble(Rmcmc, project = Rmodel)

# RUN THE MODEL
start.time <- Sys.time()
out <- runMCMC(mcmc = Cmcmc, niter = ni, nburnin = nb, nchains = nc, thin = nt,
               samplesAsCodaMCMC = T,inits = inits)
Sys.time()-start.time

Cmodel$eps.year
etc.

In the end, I managed to understand the error in calculation, I explain it below for completeness.

What I wanted was a line indicating the estimated trend of occupied sites without the year random effect.

for (k in 1:nyear){

  }

Hi Perry, thank you for the very useful suggestion.
In the end, I managed to understand the error in calculation, I explain it below for completeness.

What I wanted was a line indicating the estimated trend of occupied sites without the year random effect.
Mark Kery's model, that I used as a base, calculated this as a derived parameter:
 for (k in 1:nyear){
    logit(psi.trend[k]) <- alpha + beta.trend*year[k]
  }

In my model I added spatial autocorrelation and I was wrongly supposing that since the average of the spatial model was 0, I could exclude it from calculations.
Instead, the correct calculation needs an additional step:
  for (k in 1:nyear){
    for(i in 1:nsite){
      logit(psi.site[i,k]) <- alpha + beta.trend*year[k] + psi_rho[i] # The last one is the spatial term
    }
   psi.trend[k] <- sum(psi.site[1:nsite,k])
  }

Thank you for your support!
Mattia
